text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU pool us-west-2/generic-gpu saturating. queue_depth=1,200 (+800 in 5m), throttled_requests=420, avg_latency_token=350ms. Autoscaler attempted 3x scale but failed: rate_limit_hit / scale_cap=8 nodes. Marking P1. Please triage.
ryan_oncall: On it. Confirming impact: is this affecting hosted API only or Dedicated as well?
maria_sre: Early checks: it's the shared generic pool used by hosted inference. Dedicated customers pinned to dedicated pools are not affected. Some customer error pages reported higher latency.
anna_devops: I see autoscaler logs: "scale_request failed: quota_exceeded" then repeated "node-registration timeout". Looks like many new nodes fail to register due to driver crash on init.
leo_runtime: Uploading a snippet from the driver logs — seeing lots of CUDA/Xid 79 followed by kernel OOMs during startup. Suspect driver/kernel mismatch after last kernel module rollout.
leo_runtime: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4231: Xid's 79, 63, 31 indicate a GPU fault
[ 1234.567901] oom-killer: GpuTask killed process 4231 (runtime-worker) total-vm:12G -> oom
```
ryan_oncall: So new nodes fail on boot -> autoscaler thinks capacity is low and keeps requesting new nodes -> hits scale cap. Meanwhile queue grows. Need triage plan: 1) slow ingestion to prevent further queue growth, 2) bring up a fallback pool, 3) triage driver regression.
alex_custsuccess: Customer reports: several requests timing out for chat endpoints. One enterprise customer opened a SEV ticket. Need ETA for mitigation to set expectations.
anna_devops: I'm going to pause the autoscaler for this pool to avoid thrashing and free quota for manual rapid nodes. pausing autoscaler now. (command run: `redwood autoscaler pause --pool generic-gpu --reason "driver-init-failures"`)
ops-bot: autoscaler paused for pool generic-gpu by anna_devops at 1945612408.
maria_sre: Good. Now we should route new requests to the lower-cost-mem pool and to the cached-models pool for short-term relief. Can we update routing?
leo_runtime: Yes — I can create a temporary routing policy to favor pools: cached-gpu, small-mem-gpu, then fallback to cpu-fallback cluster. Will push rule now.
leo_runtime: ```json
{"policy": "route_by_capacity", "priorities": ["cached-gpu","small-mem-gpu","cpu-fallback"], "ttl": 10}
```
ops-bot: routing policy updated for served-api /v1/generate by leo_runtime at 1945612445.
ryan_oncall: I'm also reducing ingestion concurrency on the public API for 15m: `config set api.concurrent_requests=0.6` to cap new inflow. That should slow queue growth.
alex_custsuccess: I'll let the impacted enterprise customers know we're throttling to stabilize and that we're routing to alternate pools. ETA estimate?
leo_runtime: For a short-term mitigation: 1) route to cached-gpu and small-mem; 2) restart a subset of nodes with previous driver version (roll back kernel module) — manual provision of 2 nodes to unblock high-priority traffic. I can prepare the rollback artifact.
anna_devops: Manual node spin-up with previous driver image started. Spinning 2 nodes in us-west-2 with driver v460-rollback. Command: `infra spin-node --image gpu-image:v460-rollback --pool generic-gpu --count 2`.
ops-bot: node spin-up requested by anna_devops at 1945612501.
maria_sre: If those nodes register cleanly, we can gradually re-enable autoscaler but with a higher registration timeout and backoff. Also need to investigate why the kernel-driver rollout caused init OOMs.
leo_runtime: I ran a quick diff between driver builds. New build introduced a CUDA context allocation at startup that spikes memory usage ~11.5GB on small nodes — that pushes driver init over memory on 16GB instances when combined with other daemons. Likely the cause.
ryan_oncall: Marking immediate actions: (A) keep autoscaler paused (anna), (B) route to alternate pools (leo), (C) manual nodes with rollback (anna), (D) throttle ingestion (ryan), (E) customer comms (alex). Who owns postmortem?
maria_sre: I'll take the postmortem. We'll include timeline, root cause (driver init allocation), mitigation (rollback + routing), follow-ups (improve preflight test for driver init on smallest instance types, add registration circuit-breaker in autoscaler).
alex_custsuccess: Notifying affected customers now. Draft: "We're experiencing degraded performance due to GPU node initialisation failures; we've routed traffic to alternate pools and started manual rollbacks; ETA for stabilization ~20-40 minutes. We'll update in 15m"
anna_devops: 2 rollback nodes registered successfully and passed healthchecks. nodes: gw-node-112, gw-node-113. Logs show no Xid 79 on init.
ops-bot: node gw-node-112 registered at 1945612598. node gw-node-113 registered at 1945612604.
leo_runtime: Good. I'm starting a controlled restart of the failed nodes with the rollback image where possible and triggering an integration test against the pool.
ryan_oncall: Queue depth trending down: now 480 and decreasing. Throttled_requests at 120. Good. Will hold autoscaler paused until we confirm stability for 30m.
maria_sre: Filing postmortem ticket and tagging runtime/infra/devex. We'll also add a quick eval to the CI that boots a minimal instance with the new driver before rollout.
alex_custsuccess: Customers acknowledged the update and appreciate the quick mitigation. One customer asked for a follow-up CTO-level note; capturing that for later.
ryan_oncall: Wrapping up for handoff to night oncall in 20m — will leave detailed runbook in the incident doc. If anything regresses, page @maria_sre and @leo_runtime.
ops-bot: incident annotated: mitigation=rollback & routing; status=stabilizing; severity=P1; updated_by=ryan_oncall at 1945612715.
leo_runtime: Quick next steps: prepare fix that removes the large startup allocation, add a flag to lazy-allocate CUDA contexts. I'll open a PR and link it to the postmortem.
maria_sre: If nothing else happens, I'll transition this to a Sev-1 follow-up and schedule the blameless postmortem tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
